question: Why can household consumption be more regular than income for measuring welfare?

action.query: household consumption more regular than income measuring welfare World Bank report

action.answer: Household consumption can be more regular than income because many poor households have informal incomes that are lumpy and can vary a lot from one week to another due to seasonality, business activity, or casual labor hours. Consumption is often smoother because savings or borrowing are used to smooth out these irregular income fluctuations, so it better reflects average welfare or living standards.
